questions.q: What does Snyder recommend instead of following the news?
a: Reading books to form your own ideas
Watching more televised political debates
Sticking to one trusted news channel
Avoiding all information about politics
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends books over the news because they offer context and help you think for yourself.

questions.q: Why does Snyder say social barriers help tyranny?
a: They let tyrants isolate and distract a divided community
They make elections harder to organize
They force people to depend on the state
They slow economic growth over time
questions.why: Lesson 2 says divided communities are easier for tyranny to isolate and distract.

questions.q: What did Poland's Solidarity movement show?
a: A diverse coalition can push back against an oppressive regime
Unions should avoid working with students
Communism fell mainly because of foreign pressure
Protests succeed only when the media covers them
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes Poland's Solidarity movement uniting workers, students and intellectuals against Communism.

questions.q: How does sharing details of your life online relate to freedom?
a: The less control you have over your data, the more freedom you give up
It has no effect on your rights if your settings are private
It strengthens democracy by making everyone transparent
It only matters for people who hold public office
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that the less control you have over your personal data, the more freedom you relinquish.

questions.q: What happened to the Clinton campaign emails in 2016, per the summary?
a: They were hacked, and the fallout distracted from real issues
They were leaked by a foreign newspaper
They revealed a rigged primary vote
They were deleted before the election
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites the hacked Clinton campaign emails as an example of privacy loss and distraction.
